animal-farm-life-of-brian-history:
81 years ago today, Animal Farm was published by George Orwell. Though most famous for his seminal dystopian fiction work, Nineteen Eighty-Four, this satirical novella carries similar socio-political allegorical heft. Centered around anthropomorphic farm animals rebelling against their human farmer in hopes to create a society where all animals can be equal, free, and happy away from human interventions, things go wrong in a very human way. READ more about this great book… (1945)

According to Orwell, Animal Farm reflects events leading up to the Russian Revolution of 1917 and then on into the Stalinist era of the Soviet Union. As the Soviets fought on the side of the allies, the manuscript was initially rejected by several British and American publishers, including one of Orwell’s own, Victor Gollancz, which delayed its publication.

When it was released, it became a great commercial success as the allegiance of WWII gave way to the Cold War. Stylistically, the work shares many similarities with some of Orwell’s other works, most notably Nineteen Eighty-Four.

Orwell was committed to communicating straightforwardly, given the way that he felt words were commonly used in politics to deceive and confuse. For this reason, he is careful, in Animal Farm, to make sure the narrator speaks in an unbiased and uncomplicated fashion making the words easier to understand. The difference is seen in the way that the animals speak and interact, as the general moral animals seem to speak their minds clearly, while the wicked animals on the farm, such as a pig called Napoleon, twist language in such a way that it meets their insidious desires.

MORE Good News on this Day:

47 years ago today, Monty Python’s Life of Brian was released in theaters. Featuring troupe leader Graham Chapman as Brian Cohen, born in the stable adjacent to Jesus at Bethlehem and confusing the residents of the holy land into thinking he is the Messiah, the film was a satire on many Christian doctrines. However at the root of it, it’s just a historical setting for the group’s hilarious and innovative comedic stylings.

The film was a box office success, and the highest-grossing of any British film in the United States that year. It has remained popular and has been named the greatest comedy film of all time by several magazines and television networks, and it later received a 96% rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

Notable scenes include Brian’s attempts at spreading anti-Roman graffiti to prove himself capable of entering the resistance group the People’s Front of Judea (not to be confused, as is done constantly in the film, with the Judean People’s Front). He is caught by legionaries, but the complexity of Latin’s verb tenses and the shoddy grammar of Brian’s graffiti force the guards to correct Brian’s writing before forgetting why they approached him in the first place.

The most famous, perhaps, of all Monty Python’s musical work—Always Look on the Bright Side of Life, debuted in the film.

Reviews from critics were mostly positive on the film’s release. Movie historian Leonard Maltin reported “This will probably offend every creed and denomination equally, but it shouldn’t. The funniest and most sustained feature from Britain’s bad boys.” Vincent Canby of The New York Times called the film “the foulest-spoken biblical epic ever made, as well as the best-humored—a nonstop orgy of assaults, not on anyone’s virtue, but on the funny bone. It makes no difference that some of the routines fall flat because there are always others coming along immediately after that succeed.”

Some countries, including Ireland and Norway, banned its showing, and in a few of these, such as Italy, bans lasted over a decade. The filmmakers used the notoriety to promote the film, with posters in Sweden reading, “So funny it was banned in Norway!” (1979)

Happy Birthday to Robert De Niro, who was born in New York City 83 years ago today. The actor has appeared in over 100 films and earned 7 Academy Award nominations, winning twice—for Best Actor in Raging Bull (directed by Martin Scorsese), and for his break-out supporting role (at age 30) as the young Vito Corleone in Coppola’s epic sequel The Godfather Part II.

As a boy, he found relief from his shyness through performing, and dropped out of school at age 16 to pursue acting. “When I was around 18,” De Niro once said, “I was looking at a TV show and I said, ‘If these actors are making a living at it, and they’re not really that good, I can’t do any worse than them.'”

In 1973, De Niro began collaborating with Martin Scorsese when he appeared in the crime film Mean Streets, co-starring Harvey Keitel. Although De Niro was offered a choice of roles, Scorsese wanted De Niro to play “Johnny Boy” Civello, a small-time criminal working his way up into a local mob. Mean Streets would spawn a 5-decade-long association that produced critically acclaimed films.

The two have worked together in nine films in total, including Taxi Driver, Cape Fear, Casino, and Goodfellas. They teamed up again in 2019 with The Irishman, a biographical crime film co-starring De Niro as a hitman and Al Pacino as Jimmy Hoffa. (1943)

240 years ago today, the American folk hero Davy Crockett was born. An outstanding frontiersman, soldier in the Texas Revolution, and Tennessee congressman, he was known as the “King of the Wild Frontier”.

He actually never wore a raccoon skin cap until it was given to him by political rivals, who tried to lampoon him as an uneducated country-bumpkin, but being a confident character he put on the hat as he set off to Texas to explore new opportunities for wealth and leadership, but died in the battle over the Alamo. WATCH a short bio… (1786)

56 years ago today, the Venera 7 spacecraft was launched by the Soviet Union, and began traveling toward Venus.

Four months later, it became the first spacecraft to soft land on another planet and the first to successfully transmit data from the surface. After its parachute started to fail it stuck Venus harder than planned. The probe appeared to go silent on impact, but a few weeks later, upon a review of the tapes, 23 minutes of very weak signals were found on them. The probe transmitted the temperature at the surface of Venus to be 475 °C (887 °F) making it inhospitable to humans. (1970)

And, on this day in 1907, Pike Place Market, Seattle’s iconic tourist destination and one of the longest-running farmers markets in the US, opened.

With more than 10 million visitors exploring the 9-acre registered historic district annually, it is home to 500+ small independent businesses, including farmers, craftspeople, butchers, fish markets, shops, bakeries, restaurants, and specialty food stores. Additionally, there are more than 300 low-income housing units in the bustling year-round market, many of which are above popular storefronts.

The City chartered the Pike Place Market Preservation and Development Authority, a nonprofit public corporation, to preserve, rehabilitate and protect buildings within the Market, increase the opportunities for farm and food retailing, support small and marginal businesses, and provide services for low-income individuals. WATCH its famous Fish Throwing ritual…

Also, 67 years ago today, the American jazz trumpeter Miles Davis released Kind of Blue, the highly influential best-selling jazz record of all time. Regarded by many critics as one the greatest albums ever composed, Davis’s masterpiece influenced artists in genres from jazz to rock, to classical. Having sold nearly 5 million copies, the certified quadruple platinum LP was based on improvisation around scales—rather than chord progressions like blues or pop music—and was revolutionary in its mapping of uncharted territory, creating a new language for music based on the modal theory.

Several of the musicians playing with Miles Davis on the album are now legendary in their own right: tenor saxophonist John Coltrane; alto saxophonist Julian ‘Cannonball’ Adderley; pianists Bill Evans and Wynton Kelly; bassist Paul Chambers; and drummer Jimmy Cobb.

As was Davis’s penchant, he called for almost no rehearsal and the musicians had little idea what they were to record. As described in the original liner notes by pianist Bill Evans, Davis had only given the band sketches of scales and melody lines on which to improvise. Davis gave brief instructions in studio for each of the five tracks. The persistent legend that the entire album was recorded in one pass is untrue. It was, however, recorded in two days. Coltrane said it was music “made in heaven”—a gift to the world. (1959)

Miles, who was born in Illinois, died in 1991 at the age of 65 and was buried with one of his trumpets in a cemetery in The Bronx near Duke Ellington’s gravesite. HEAR the opening track, So What…

On this day in 1945, Indonesia declared its Independence from the Netherlands. It was 10:00 AM on a Friday that Mohammad Hatta and Sukarno went on the radio at the latter’s house in central Jakarta, and announced that Indonesia would no longer accept orders, laws, or jurisdiction issued by Holland, sparking the 4-year Indonesian Revolution of Independence.

Throughout the 1920s and 1930s, three Indonesian revolutionaries, Mohammad Hatta,  Sukarno, and Sutan Sjahrir, repeatedly tried to build a revolutionary movement that looked to unite all of the Dutch East Indies, and not at the sometimes-local allegiance to a particular island. They formed political parties or revolutionary groups aimed at achieving independence through non-cooperation with the Dutch, and each spent several stints in prison and exile.

The detention of these nationalist figures effectively ended the non-cooperation movement, and in December 1935 the moderate Indonesian National Union and another party called Budi Utomo merged to form the Great Indonesia Party (Parindra), which aimed to work with the Dutch to achieve Indonesian independence.

After the outbreak of the Second World War, the Dutch were in no position to spend political effort to reform the governmental situation on Indonesia before the Japanese swept in and took control of the whole archipelago. There, administration of the major islands was managed by Japanese troops, but as the tide turned against Japan’s expansion across Asia, the need to free up those forces saw Hatta, Sukarno, and Sjahrir invited to return by the Japanese, who sought to create an independence movement through the old revolutionaries.

The Japanese decided to grant Indonesian independence to create problems for the Dutch when they reoccupied their colony. At a meeting in Singapore at the end of July, it was decided that Java would become independent at the end of September, followed by other areas. After internal political squabbling about the best way to go about it, Sukarno and Hatta, believed by some as the only men with enough gravitas to make the declaration, read aloud a very simple message:

“We the people of Indonesia hereby declare the independence of Indonesia. Matters concerning the transfer of power and other matters will be executed in an orderly manner and in the shortest possible time.”

earthquake-in-tibet-kills-at-least-16:
A powerful earthquake of magnitude 7.0 struck the mountainous Nagqu region of Tibet on Thursday night, killing at least 16 people, injuring dozens more, and wiping out hundreds of buildings.

According to Chinese state media, the quake struck at around 10:33 p.m. local time, centered about 120 miles from the city of Nagqu. It was the most powerful quake recorded in the region in five years. The initial 7.0 quake was followed by at least seven aftershocks, the most powerful of which was measured at 5.2 magnitude.

Video clips from Nagqu showed frightened residents fleeing into the streets as buildings shook around them:

Local media said 339 homes and 20 livestock sheds were destroyed. Authorities reported 16 fatalities and 54 injuries, while more than 12,400 people were relocated. Some of those people took shelter in cars and tents because they feared the aftershocks could collapse more buildings. Temperatures in that part of Tibet fall well below zero at night.

Chinese state media reported that some 2,000 prefabricated houses, 3,400 tents, and 2,000 folding beds have been sent to the area, along with winter clothing and other supplies.

Over 1,600 search and rescue personnel were deployed through the area after the quake, and the operation grew to over 5,000 by Friday afternoon.

Power, communications, and railroad travel have been knocked out in some of the affected areas, and snow is forecast over the next few days, complicating rescue efforts. Water and electricity have been disrupted through the surrounding township of Maru, which has a little over 7,600 residents, according to the most recent census.

The BBC noted that since occupied Tibet is tightly controlled by the Chinese government and foreign media is restricted, most news about the quake is coming from Chinese state media.

Chinese dictator Xi Jinping issued a statement on Friday calling for “all-out search and rescue efforts for the missing, and prompt medical treatment for the injured.” Premier Li Qiang made a similar statement.

A Los Angeles outreach worker has revealed the sickening depths swindlers will sink to in order to lure homeless addicts to California detox centers, after a pair of accused fraudsters were charged by federal authorities in a $1.6 billion drug rehab scheme.Federal prosecutors busted David Young, 71, and his son Nathan Young, 39, who are accused of using “body brokers” to recruit at least 6,000 junkies — many from out of state — to enter Golden State rehabilitation clinics as part of an alleged insurance scam.LA-based homeless advocate and outreach worker Lang Martinez said the sickening scam the Youngs are accused of is all too commonplace on Skid Row, while revealing more of the disgusting tricks that fraudsters employ to maximize their profits.

The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now.

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

Never miss a story

“Los Angeles is definitely a hot spot for this sort of thing,” said Martinez, who lived homeless on Skid Row before getting sober in 2018 and turning his life around. “First, they’ll find someone caught up in addiction. Then, they’ll give you a little bit of money.”

Next, said Martinez, body broker cons will obtain an ID from a victim, and get them insurance, so that they can be admitted to a rehab center on the insurer’s dime, about a week later.

“They have insiders with the insurance companies, your top insurance companies,” said Martinez of such cons. “They’ll grease their palms, and then what they’ll do is they’ll backdate homeboy’s insurance.”

The body brokers’ spiel next goes something like this: “’Got you a spot, man. I’m gonna put you on a plane, and I’m gonna fly you out to this place,’” Martinez said

“It happens all over the country,” he added. “Get you in the car. Put you on a plane.”

But once there, addicts may realize they’re not getting help at all, but just ripoffs like those alleged to have occurred at the Youngs’ bogus rehabs, such as Zoom meetings with hundreds of attendees and no treatment, or trips to the movies disguised as group therapy.

Worse, said Martinez, body brokers often pull sobers addicts out of rehab, ply them with cash and drugs, and encourage a relapse. Then, they’ll readmit them at another rehabilitation front, collecting another placement fee to drive up their profits.

“A lot of these people die,” said Martinez of addicts victimized in this way.

“They relapse you again, and then I put you in another program,” he said. “That’s how the brokering works.”

Martinez said hundreds of homeless addicts wandering Skid Row probably landed there under such schemes.

“When you turn human suffering into a business, you’ve lost your humanity,” he added. “What is happening to our unhoused and our most vulnerable individuals through body brokering is not recovery – it’s exploitation.”

The practice grabbed headlines this week in the case of the Youngs, who are accused of using body brokers including accused Greenville, Texas couple Honey and Cody Phipps, to mercilessly target homeless addicts and recycle them through their drug facilities.

Justice Department prosecutors say the defendants pocketed more than $210 million in the six-year scheme that Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald called “the largest the largest sober home fraud scheme the Department has ever prosecuted.”

Both Youngs and both Phipps were arrested in a sweeping anti-healthcare fraud investigation in California that federal authorities unveiled in Los Angeles Thursday.

To execute the complex con, the Youngs ordered the Phipps and other body brokers to travel to various states to find homeless addicts, get them insured and enroll them at the Youngs’ rehabs in LA, San Diego, the Bay Area and elsewhere, court papers say.

Credit card records showed that victims were flown in from Las Vegas, Cleveland, and Birmingham, Ala., according to court papers.

The body brokers offered addicts kickbacks to enroll at the Youngs’ rehabs, “including money, drugs, free airline flights, free or nearly-free accommodations at highly desirable locations, including luxury apartments and houses in” Los Angeles, prosecutors say.

Sometimes, victims were coached “to fabricate and exaggerate their symptoms and substance addictions during intake,” or encouraged to use drugs or alcohol so that they would not pass a urine drug test,” and would be eligible for rehab, court papers state.

Once inside the Youngs’ network of rehab homes, the patients were cycled through different types of treatment centers that corresponded to different levels of sobriety, so the fraudsters could maximize their profits, prosecutors charge.

To keep their victims as long as possible, the Youngs had such addicts “drugged with medication, cut off from communication with family members, prevented from accessing their belongings, and physically blocked from leaving,” according to court papers.

First Assistant US Attorney Bill Essayli said the scheme was particularly distressing in light of California’s homelessness problem.

“These body brokers brought vulnerable people here with false promises of treatment, worsening California’s drug-addicted homelessness crisis,” he said. “We will hold accountable those who turn addiction and human suffering into a business.”

“These body brokers brought vulnerable people here with false promises of treatment, worsening California’s drug-addicted homelessness crisis,” he said. “We will hold accountable those who turn addiction and human suffering into a business.”

New Jersey’s notorious “Tan Mom” said she was questioned by “racist” ICE agents about whether she’s a US citizen — simply because her skin is so dark.

Patricia Krentcil — who gained notoriety when she was arrested for allegedly bringing her 5-year-old daughter into a tanning bed in 2012 — told the podcast Light she was nearly cuffed while at a restaurant with friends, although she didn’t specify where or when it allegedly happened.

“As we were walking out, the ICE people stopped me and they asked me ‘am I an American citizen,’ and I’m like, ‘yes.’ It blew my mind,” she said.

“Because I was so tan they were about to handcuff me and take me away to God knows where. Cause once you get in those trucks, you don’t know where you’re going anymore.”

The aging over-bronzed bombshell also slammed President Trump for supporting “all this nonsense.”

“I was scared but I held my own and I got out of the situation — but they’re very racist about color and nationality,” she added.

ICE has previously denied that it engages in unconstitutional racial profiling during enforcement operations.

In April 2012, Krentcil was arrested and charged with second-degree child endangerment after her daughter arrived at school with sunburns.

Charges were dropped the following February when an Essex County grand jury refused to indict her.

The extreme tanning buff has since become a podcast host herself and now lives in — where else? — the Sunshine State.

Santa Monica’s most iconic sign came down Friday in a bid to restore it to its old glory, and the California Post was there to capture the dismantling.

The 20-foot blue neon arch, a fixture above the entrance of the Santa Monica Pier since 1941, will be hauled away and shipped to Las Vegas as Santa Monica embarks on a multimillion-dollar bridge overhaul.

The vintage sign could remain out of sight for nearly a year while crews replace the 87-year-old bridge beneath it. The sign will be restored by YESCO, an American manufacturer that also worked on the Welcome to Fabulous Las Vegas sign, before returning to its perch atop the rebuilt bridge, according to the city.

“The sign is not being removed permanently or replaced,” the City of Santa Monica website reads. “It is being refurbished and its historic character will remain intact.”

“It will be returned — looking better than ever — to its rightful place at the top of the bridge when construction is complete, expected in late 2027.”

“Few sights are as instantly recognizable as the Santa Monica Pier sign, and generations of residents and visitors have memories tied to seeing it at the entrance to the Pier,” Mayor Caroline Torosis said in a statement.

“This careful refurbishment will preserve the sign’s history while ensuring this beloved landmark can continue welcoming people to the Pier for decades to come. And in the meantime, the temporary sign will continue to offer visitors the opportunity to capture that quintessential Santa Monica Pier moment.”

That temporary sign is a half-scale replica installed along the temporary walkway.

The whole remake is part of a $35.5 million bridge replacement project awarded to Shimmick Construction Company.

The taxpayer-funded overhaul will replace the aging connection between the pier and city streets with a new bridge built to modern seismic standards, along with wider pedestrian sidewalks and redesigned walkways.

The new structure is expected to have a 70-year service life.

Photos captured workers taking the sign down on Friday, but in reality, it was a multi-day process.

Workers used a crane and temporary support structures to dismantle the Santa Monica Pier sign in sections. Preparation, equipment setup and removal of the sign’s neon tubing happened Tuesday.

The sign’s upper crown was scheduled to be removed this past Wednesday, followed by the main portion of the sign Thursday.

The sign will be wrapped and loaded onto transport vehicles, with transportation expected to begin Oct. 26. Once in Vegas, the restoration work will include repairing neon tubing, removing rust, repainting the sign and its supporting components and completing structural repairs, officials said.

Removal work was scheduled from 5 a.m. to 3 p.m. Tuesday through Saturday, with one lane of Ocean Avenue near the pier entrance closed during work hours.

The public was able to watch the removal from two designated viewing areas: the southern edge of Palisades Park and the northeast side of the pier entrance at Ocean Avenue and Colorado Avenue.

The neon gateway dates back to June 17, 1941, when it was unveiled by the Santa Monica Pier Business Men’s Association. It was later declared a historic landmark by the State of California Department of Parks and Recreation in 1996.

brazil-flavio-bolsonaro-runoff-2026:
An overwhelming majority of polls in Brazil indicate that conservative Senator Flávio Bolsonaro is ahead of incumbent socialist President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva as the nation is hours away from the October 25 runoff election.

Over 158 million Brazilian voters are called to head to the polls on Sunday to choose between Bolsonaro and Lula as their president for the next four years. On Friday morning, the Brazilian outlet Poder 360 published a summary containing the results of the latest 17 surveys conducted by the nation’s top polling firms.

Out of the total, Sen. Bolsonaro appears numerically ahead in 15 out of the 17 polls, while Lula only appears as the winner in a poll conducted by the firm Vox Brasil. Both candidates appear tied with 50 percent each in the latest poll conducted by the left-leaning Datafolha firm. All 17 polls were conducted across different dates throughout mid-October.

Although Bolsonaro is ahead in the majority of the polls, the outlet observed that the percentage differences are “within the margin of error,” indicating the possibility of a close race between the candidates on Sunday. The conservative senator defied first-round polling and defeated Lula in the October 4 first round of the presidential election. However, he did not obtain the required 50 percent majority of the votes to automatically in the first round, triggering the upcoming Sunday runoff. The October 4 election notably featured 13 different presidential candidates on the ballot.

The final chapter of the presidential runoff campaign was marked by the first debate between Bolsonaro and Lula on Sunday, which mainstream media catalogued as “chaotic.” A second and final debate is scheduled to take place in Rio de Janeiro on Friday night (local time).

The yet-to-occur debate, however, was marked by a weeklong controversy that arose after Lula claimed that he would not allow Bolsonaro on stage unless he complied with his demands to disclose an extensive amount of financial, tax, and phone call information about his entire family — issuing a “challenge” to Bolsonaro to authorize the TSE to publish the information if he wanted to debate him again. Lula justified his demand on the grounds that the president of the republic could not debate a “thief.”

Bolsonaro not only agreed to Lula’s challenge, but presented a counter-challenge, daring Lula to disclose his own corporate credit card expenditures in addition to the financial, tax, and phone call records of the Lula family. Bolsonaro affirmed that his counter-challenge sought to “break out the endless cycle that serves no purpose.”

“Let us begin, then, with what is public. With that which is public by nature, information that should never be hidden from public view and that does not fall under the fundamental guarantee of individual privacy,” Bolsonaro reportedly detailed in the formal petition.

“Expenses charged to the Presidency of the Republic’s corporate credit card are paid for with taxpayer money, and an audit by the Federal Court of Accounts found that 99.55 percent of them were classified as confidential or restricted between January 2023 and April 2025,” the document continued.

The controversy over the mutual disclosure of financial information led to a rapid-fire legal back and forth between the Bolsonaro and Lula campaigns at Brazil’s top electoral authority, the Superior Electoral Tribunal (TSE). Per CNN Brasil, the Lula campaign submitted all the information to the TSE, including the corporate credit card expense reports, while the Bolsonaro campaign complied with the “challenge” and submitted a document signed by the senator authorizing the disclosure of the information. At press time Friday morning, none of the information surrounding the controversy has reportedly been disclosed to the public.

On Thursday evening, Brazilian Supreme Court Justice André Mendonça stated that both presidential campaigns may reveal the information on their own without the need of the judiciary, affirming that it is not up to the TSE to define the disclosure. According to Globonews, Justice Mendonça stated that bank statements are available at the respective financial institutions “with broad and easy access for each account holder.” Income tax statements can be collected on the Brazilian Federal Revenue Service’s website, while phone records can be obtained from the corresponding telecommunications operator.

Mendoça nevertheless highlighted that voluntary data disclosure do not replace an official verification by the relevant authorities, under judicial oversight, to analyze possible inconsistencies.

Despite Lula conditioning the debate on his demands, and the controversy surrounding the “challenge” issued by the socialist president, preparations for the final debate reportedly remain on schedule at press time. The event will be hosted and broadcast live on Friday night by TV Globo. Both candidates are expected to attend the debate before bringing their campaigns to a close in the next hours ahead of Sunday’s runoff.

Brazilian outlets noted that the TV Globo debate will have a different format from the first one, hosted by TV Bandeirantes. Per O Globo, the upcoming debate will be structured in four blocks. In every block, one of the candidates must formulate a question to his opponent, with three minutes of speaking per round. For the second and third blocks, the candidates can choose from question already defined by the organizers.

The fourth and final block will be a “free subject,” one in which every candidate will have eight minutes at their disposal to speak his mind.

Unlike the first debate, which allowed candidates to freely walk across the stage, only the speaking candidate will be allowed to move around during the first three blocks. In the fourth and final block, the candidates will be allowed to freely move but only on their respective sides of the stage. According to Poder 360, both the Bolsonaro and Lula campaigns acknowledged that “mistakes” were committed by the two candidates during the first debate, with Lula deeming Bolsonaro’s movements and gestures while the president spoke “disrespectful.”
